Expected range of n standard normal variables

Source: R/sgp-denominators-helpers.R
expected_range_normal.Rd

Computes E[X_(n) - X_(1)], the expected range of n iid standard normal variables, via numerical integration of the exact formula:

Usage

expected_range_normal(n)

Arguments

n

Integer or numeric scalar, >= 2. Number of standard normal variables (i.e., number of teams in the league).

Value

Numeric scalar. The expected range E[X_(n) - X_(1)].

Details

integral_{-Inf}^{Inf} [ 1 - Phi(x)^n - (1 - Phi(x))^n ] dx

This quantity is used by the "sd" method of sgp_denominators() to convert the within-year standard deviation of category totals into a denominator expressed in standings-gap units.

The integral is evaluated by stats::integrate() with default tolerance. Results are stable to better than 1e-3 for all n >= 2.

Verified anchors from Monte Carlo and analytical integration:

n = 103.0776
n = 123.2587
n = 153.4718
n = 203.7350

See also

sgp_denominators()

Examples

expected_range_normal(10)  # 3.0776
#> [1] 3.077505
expected_range_normal(12)  # 3.2587
#> [1] 3.258455
expected_range_normal(15)  # 3.4718
#> [1] 3.471827
